response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net, COUNT(*) AS rec_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY dealedge) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, avg_net AS avg_net_fee_rate, rec_count AS record_count, avg_net - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: High-rate means feerate strictly greater than 0.0009 (a fee exactly at the cutoff is excluded).

Record count is the number of matched high-rate fee rows in the group (COUNT(*)), including rows whose net rate is null. The average skips those rows because a null feerate or rebrate makes the difference null.
The side average is the unweighted mean of the group averages for that side. Groups with a null average are ignored in that mean and cannot qualify.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rate means feerate at or above 0.0009 (cutoff inclusive).
